statements.text: In a 16-patient subset, MSBM agreed with the myChoice CDx assay in only 31% of cases.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In a subset (n = 16), MSBM showed 81% concordance with myChoice CDx and correlated with genomic instability scores (R = 0.63).
statements.note: The reported concordance in that subset was 81%, not 31%.

statements.text: The 45 patients on olaparib reached a median progression-free survival of 22.3 months, beating the prespecified 9-month threshold at p < 0.001.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The olaparib arm (n = 45) showed a median PFS of 22.3 months, significantly exceeding the 9-month threshold (p < 0.001), meeting the primary endpoint.
statements.note: This is the trial's primary endpoint result, reported exactly these values.

statements.text: Overall survival was longer in the olaparib arm than in the placebo arm.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The placebo arm (n = 11) with a median PFS of 16.7 months was not powered for comparison.
statements.note: Only progression-free survival is reported for either arm; overall survival is never mentioned.

statements.text: MSBM calls homologous recombination deficiency from whole-exome features such as tumor-BRCA status and Mutational Signature 3 similarity, without using genomic scars.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The MSBM was designed to integrate three whole-exome sequencing-derived features without using genomic scars: tumor-BRCA mutation status, Mutational Signature 3 similarity score > 0.5, or score > 0.25 without CCNE1 amplification.
statements.note: The abstract describes exactly this scar-free, exome-based biomarker design.

statements.text: Baseline circulating tumor DNA was detectable in 85% of the soft tissue sarcoma patients studied.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Personalized ctDNA profiling detected baseline ctDNA in 85% of patients.
statements.note: The detection rate of 85% at baseline is reported directly.

statements.text: Patients given pembrolizumab showed a smaller drop in ctDNA levels after neoadjuvant therapy than those who were not.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients treated with pembrolizumab, who had significantly better disease-free survival, had a greater decrease in their ctDNA levels after neoadjuvant therapy.
statements.note: The pembrolizumab-treated patients had a greater, not smaller, decrease in ctDNA.

statements.text: Baseline ctDNA levels were higher in sarcomas arising in the extremities than in truncal sarcomas.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Baseline ctDNA levels correlated with tumor size, grade 3 disease, and expression of genes related to hypoxia and the cell cycle.
statements.note: The correlates of baseline ctDNA are listed, but tumor anatomic site is never among them.

statements.text: Patients with more than one tumor clone detected in plasma after surgery had worse outcomes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: patients with multiple tumor clones detected by ctDNA analysis after surgery had inferior outcomes
statements.note: Multiclonal postsurgical ctDNA is reported as marking inferior outcomes.

statements.text: Patients whose plasma KRAS mutation was detected had shorter overall survival than those without a detectable mutation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our prediction system effectively stratified patients by the likelihood of KRAS mutation detection, offering a practical tool for selecting candidates for liquid biopsy.
statements.note: The study models only the probability of detecting KRAS and reports no survival comparison.

statements.text: Liver metastasis, multiple metastatic sites and disease progression were each independent predictors of successful KRAS detection.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Multivariate analysis revealed that liver metastasis, multiple metastatic sites, and disease progression were significant predictors of successful KRAS mutation detection.
statements.note: These are exactly the three significant predictors from the multivariate model.

statements.text: The nomogram achieved 70% sensitivity, 90.9% specificity and an area under the curve of 0.83.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with a sensitivity of 70%, specificity of 90.9%, and area under curve of 0.83
statements.note: These three performance figures are reported for the nomogram and its ROC curve.

statements.text: The prediction model was derived from 320 patients who underwent ctDNA testing between 2019 and 2024.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We retrospectively analyzed 32 patients who underwent ctDNA testing from 2019 to 2024
statements.note: The cohort was 32 patients, a tenth of the number claimed.

statements.text: HNF4A expression is inversely regulated by nearby liver-specific accessible transposable elements, which drives liver cancer cell proliferation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our findings reveal that the expression of HNF4A is inversely regulated by proximate liver-TEs, which facilitates liver cancer cell proliferation.
statements.note: This inverse regulation and its pro-proliferative consequence are the study's central finding.

statements.text: Pharmacological KDM1A inhibition shrank tumors in mouse models of hepatocellular carcinoma.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In conclusion, this study uncovers a liver-TE/KDM1A/HNF4A regulatory axis that promotes liver cancer growth and highlights KDM1A as a promising therapeutic target.
statements.note: Calling KDM1A a promising target says nothing about any inhibitor or animal experiment, which the abstract never reports.

statements.text: KDM1A raises H3K4 methylation at liver-TEs and thereby increases HNF4A expression.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: KDM1A negatively influences the methylation of histone H3 Lys4 (H3K4) of liver-TEs, resulting in the epigenetic silencing of HNF4A expression.
statements.note: KDM1A lowers H3K4 methylation and silences HNF4A, the opposite of this statement.

statements.text: The histone demethylase KDM1A is the dominant occupant of liver-specific accessible transposable elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Mechanistically, liver-TEs are predominantly occupied by the histone demethylase, KDM1A.
statements.note: Predominant KDM1A occupancy of liver-TEs is stated as the mechanism.

statements.text: BayVarC reached a limit of detection of 0.1% while holding false positives to 0.05 per kilobase.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: BayVarC can effectively detect low frequency variants while maintaining low false positive rate (0.05 FP/KB). Meanwhile, it achieves Limit of Detection (LoD) as low as 0.1%.
statements.note: Both performance figures are reported for the caller.

statements.text: In simulation and in-vitro testing, BayVarC performed worse than existing state-of-the-art variant callers.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Detailed in-silico simulation and in-vitro experiments demonstrated BayVarC’ superior performance over existing state-of-the-art tools.
statements.note: Those same experiments are reported to show superior, not inferior, performance.

statements.text: BayVarC quantifies noise separately at each locus by Bayesian inference, separating technical noise from genuine low-frequency cancer variants.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: It applies Bayesian inference to accurately quantify noise level in a locus-specific manner, enabling the discrimination between technical noise and low-frequency cancer variants.
statements.note: This locus-specific Bayesian noise model is how the tool is described to work.

statements.text: BayVarC analyses samples faster than the variant callers it was benchmarked against.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Detailed in-silico simulation and in-vitro experiments demonstrated BayVarC’ superior performance over existing state-of-the-art tools.
statements.note: Superiority is claimed for variant-calling accuracy; runtime and computational cost are never mentioned.

statements.text: A four-lncRNA signature split glioma patients into high- and low-risk groups, with worse prognosis in the high-risk group.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A 4-lncRNA signature effectively stratified patients into high-risk and low-risk groups. The prognosis of the high-risk group is worse.
statements.note: The signature's composition and the direction of the prognostic difference are both reported.

statements.text: High-risk patients were older at diagnosis than low-risk patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: A 4-lncRNA signature effectively stratified patients into high-risk and low-risk groups. The prognosis of the high-risk group is worse.
statements.note: The risk groups are compared on prognosis and immune features only; patient age is never mentioned.

statements.text: The risk score lost its predictive power in the independent CGGA validation cohort.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In multivariate analysis, a risk score can independently predict the prognosis and has a robust prediction efficiency in the CGGA external verification set.
statements.note: The risk score is reported to retain robust predictive efficiency in the CGGA set.

statements.text: High-risk patients had more M2 macrophage infiltration, higher PD-L1 expression and fewer infiltrating CD8+ T cells.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The infiltration of immunosuppressive cells, such as M2 macrophages, increased the expression of immune checkpoints, such as PD-L1, increased, and the infiltration of CD8 + T cells decreased in high-risk patients.
statements.note: All three immune features are reported in this direction for the high-risk group.

statements.text: For tumor mutational burden, the correlation between whole-exome sequencing and the targeted panel was 57%.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: For TMB measurement, the correlation coefficient between whole-exome sequencing and our targeted panel was 97%.
statements.note: The reported correlation coefficient was 97%, not 57%.

statements.text: Personalizing ctDNA tracking with mutations found by comprehensive genomic profiling detected ctDNA in plasma in 79% of cases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: When CGP-informed mutations were used to personalize ctDNA tracking, the detection rate of ctDNA in liquid biopsy was 79%
statements.note: The 79% ctDNA detection rate with CGP-informed tracking is reported directly.

statements.text: The assay detected variants at allele frequencies below 0.01%.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Reference standards were used to evaluate limit of detection (LOD), concordance, sensitivity, specificity and precision of the assay
statements.note: Limit of detection is listed as something evaluated, but no allele-frequency value is ever given.

statements.text: Against the TruSight Oncology 500 assay, concordance was 100% for somatic variants, 89% for tumor mutational burden and 98% for microsatellite instability.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The concordance between our assay and the TruSight Oncology 500 assay for detection of somatic variants, TMB and MSI measurement was 100%, 89% and 98% respectively.
statements.note: These are the three concordance figures reported for that comparison.

statements.text: Over a median follow-up of 18 months, seven of the twenty patients progressed and three died.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: During a median follow-up of 18 months, seven (35%) patients progressed and three (15%) died.
statements.note: The event counts and follow-up duration are reported exactly.

statements.text: Patients with higher cfDNA levels had larger primary tumors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Multivariate analysis demonstrated that cfDNA levels three months after RNU are a significant predictor of tumor progression (HR = 1.085; p = 0.006) and CSS (HR = 1.168; p = 0.029).
statements.note: cfDNA is related only to progression and cancer-specific survival; no tumor-size or stage comparison is reported.

statements.text: cfDNA concentration three months after radical nephroureterectomy independently predicted both tumor progression and cancer-specific survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Multivariate analysis demonstrated that cfDNA levels three months after RNU are a significant predictor of tumor progression (HR = 1.085; p = 0.006) and CSS (HR = 1.168; p = 0.029).
statements.note: Both associations were significant in the multivariate analysis.

statements.text: Circulating tumor cell counts were also significantly associated with tumor progression in this cohort.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: No associations were found between CTC enumeration and ctDNA status with any of the clinical outcomes evaluated.
statements.note: CTC enumeration showed no association with any clinical outcome.

statements.text: Mortality was higher among patients whose pathogens were missed by standard of care testing.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Compared to patients with Category One or Two organisms identified by both SOC and KT-BAL (n = 68), patients with organisms identified by KT-BAL alone (n = 87) had significantly more cumulative intubation days (11 [5, 20] days vs. 15 [8, 32] days, p = 0.035).
statements.note: The only outcome compared between these groups is cumulative intubation days; mortality is never reported.

statements.text: Beyond standard of care, mcfDNA sequencing of lavage fluid added 18 Category One and 138 Category Two organisms in pneumonia patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In pneumonia patients, KT-BAL yielded 18 additional Category One organisms, 138 additional Category Two organisms, and 313 additional Category Three organisms compared to SOC.
statements.note: These additional-organism counts by category are reported directly.

statements.text: Patients whose organisms were found only by KT-BAL spent significantly fewer days intubated than those whose organisms were found by both methods.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Compared to patients with Category One or Two organisms identified by both SOC and KT-BAL (n = 68), patients with organisms identified by KT-BAL alone (n = 87) had significantly more cumulative intubation days (11 [5, 20] days vs. 15 [8, 32] days, p = 0.035).
statements.note: The KT-BAL-only group had significantly more, not fewer, intubation days.

statements.text: The study analysed 228 bronchoalveolar lavage samples drawn from 155 patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 228 BAL fluid samples from 155 patients were analyzed.
statements.note: These sample and patient counts are stated at the start of the findings.

statements.text: Every isolate carried at least one resistance gene and one plasmid replicon, with 37 resistance genes and 27 replicons seen across the collection.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: All E. coli isolates were positive for at least one antibiotic resistance gene and plasmid replicon, with 37 resistance genes and 27 plasmid replicons detected among the isolates.
statements.note: Both the universal positivity and the gene and replicon counts are reported.

statements.text: Intact prophages were rare, found in only a small minority of the isolates.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Most isolates (95%) harbored at least one intact phage, and as many as seven intact phages were identified in one isolate.
statements.note: Intact phages were present in 95% of isolates, not a small minority.

statements.text: No extended-spectrum beta-lactamase genes were found, and bla CMY-2 was the most common beta-lactamase gene.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: While no ESBL genes were detected, bla CMY-2 was the most common β-lactamase gene, and bla TEM and bla CARB-2 were also identified.
statements.note: The absence of ESBL genes and the predominance of bla CMY-2 are both reported.

statements.text: Resistance gene content increased in isolates collected later within the 2001 to 2012 period.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This retrospective study also enables comparisons of resistance genes and mobile genetic elements from more recent E. coli isolates associated with poultry to aid in understanding the trends of both antibiotic resistance phenotypes and genotypes in the poultry setting over time.
statements.note: Temporal trends are framed as something the data enable; no change over the sampling years is reported.

statements.text: NovoCAST showed a 500-fold activity increase over the parental PmcCAST along with sharply defined integration profiles.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: NovoCAST exhibits sharply defined integration profiles, a 500-fold increase in activity relative to the parental PmcCAST, and general programmability.
statements.note: Both the 500-fold gain and the sharp integration profiles are reported.

statements.text: The transposition machinery was reconfigured to interface with Cas12 rather than Cas9.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Our strategy exploits the modular architecture of CRISPR-associated transposons (CASTs), reconfiguring their conserved transposition machinery to interface with widely adopted Cas9.
statements.note: The machinery was redesigned to interface with Cas9.

statements.text: Integration by NovoCAST was more precise in human cells than in bacterial cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Finally, we demonstrate robust programmable genomic integration in human cells highlighting its broad potential applications in research and therapeutics.
statements.note: Human-cell integration is reported on its own, with no bacterial comparison.

statements.text: NovoCAST cuts the CAST architecture from eight proteins to four, the fewest reported for such a system.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The resulting system, which we call NovoCAST, simplifies the CAST architecture from eight distinct proteins to four, establishing the simplest CAST described to date.
statements.note: The eight-to-four simplification and the claim of being the simplest CAST are stated.

statements.text: The assay tested 1,214 variants across six regulatory regions of CYP3A4.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We assayed 1,214 variants across six CYP3A4 regulatory regions, integrating variants from global populations, cancer genomes, and archaic humans.
statements.note: The variant count and the number of regulatory regions are reported exactly.

statements.text: Variants taken from archaic human genomes had larger regulatory effects than variants from present-day populations.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We assayed 1,214 variants across six CYP3A4 regulatory regions, integrating variants from global populations, cancer genomes, and archaic humans.
statements.note: The three variant sources are listed, but their effect sizes are never compared with each other.

statements.text: Most of the variants tested strongly altered regulatory activity, with only a handful having little effect.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Most variants exerted modest to no effects on regulatory activity, consistent with strong functional constraint at the CYP3A4 locus.
statements.note: Most variants had modest or no effect, the reverse of this statement.

statements.text: A minority of variants did have significant regulatory impact, including some linked to altered drug response and cancer severity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: However, we identified a subset of variants with significant regulatory impact, including variants that could be associated with altered drug response and cancer severity.
statements.note: A subset of high-impact variants with these possible associations is reported.

statements.text: The isolates came from patients with recurrent urinary tract infections at a single hospital.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Five biofilm-forming MDR UPEC isolates were selected for whole-genome sequencing (WGS) using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform.
statements.note: How and where the five isolates were obtained is never described.

statements.text: Five biofilm-forming multidrug-resistant UPEC isolates were whole-genome sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Five biofilm-forming MDR UPEC isolates were selected for whole-genome sequencing (WGS) using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform.
statements.note: The number of isolates and the sequencing platform are stated in the methods.

statements.text: All of the isolates carried virulence genes tied to adhesion, immune evasion and biofilm formation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: All isolates harbored virulence genes associated with adhesion, immune evasion, and biofilm formation.
statements.note: This universal virulence gene content is reported for the isolates.

statements.text: The plasmids detected across the isolates were predominantly IncH-type.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Mobile genetic elements, particularly IncF-type plasmids and insertion sequences, were detected across isolates, suggesting a role in horizontal gene transfer of resistance traits.
statements.note: The plasmids detected across isolates were IncF-type.

statements.text: DmTNP-CTD homologs were spread across the animal kingdom, while THAP9-CTD homologs were confined to arthropods.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: THAP9-CTD homologs were more widely distributed throughout the animal kingdom in comparison to DmTNP-CTD homologs which were restricted to arthropods.
statements.note: The distributions are the other way round: THAP9-CTD homologs are widespread and DmTNP-CTD homologs are arthropod-restricted.

statements.text: The two C-terminal domains share three conserved hydrophobic helical regions predicted to form a common core.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: they both surprisingly share similar secondary structure elements consisting of three conserved helical regions made of hydrophobic residues that are predicted to make up a conserved core
statements.note: The shared three-helix hydrophobic core is reported for both CTDs.

statements.text: THAP9 is expressed at its highest level in human testis.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: THAP9 is a transposable element-derived gene which encodes a protein that is homologous to the active Drosophila P-element transposase (DmTNP).
statements.note: The abstract covers THAP9's origin, domain and activity but says nothing about its expression pattern in tissues.

statements.text: Truncation mutants lacking the C-terminal domain still carried out DNA excision and integration for both THAP9 and DmTNP.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Interestingly both THAP9 and DmTNP truncation mutants are still capable of DNA excision and integration, suggesting that their respective CTDs are not essential for DNA transposition.
statements.note: Both truncation mutants retained excision and integration activity.

statements.text: Two clinical Pseudomonas fulva strains carried transferable megaplasmids harbouring both bla VIM-24 and tmexCD3-toprJ3.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Clinical P. fulva strains, ZDHY316 and ZDHY414, with transferable megaplasmids co-carrying bla VIM-24 and tmexCD3-toprJ3.
statements.note: Two named strains with megaplasmids co-carrying these two determinants are reported.

statements.text: Patients infected with these strains were treated successfully with ceftazidime-avibactam.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The horizontal transfer potential of this megaplasmid poses a significant challenge to clinical infection control.
statements.note: Infection-control risk is discussed, but patient treatment and outcomes are never reported.

statements.text: pJBCL41-like megaplasmids were found to be evolving toward carrying more resistance genes and mobile genetic elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Phylogenetic analysis of pJBCL41-like megaplasmids showed their evolution towards carrying more drug-resistance genes and mobile genetic elements.
statements.note: This evolutionary trend is the reported result of the megaplasmid phylogeny.

statements.text: Among countries, China contributed the fewest clinically isolated P. fulva strains in the phylogenetic analysis.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Phylogenetic analysis of P. fulva strains showed that China is the country with the most P. fulva isolated clinically, with strains prevalent and evolving in hospitals.
statements.note: China had the most clinically isolated P. fulva, not the fewest.

statements.text: Acquired high tumor mutational burden was most common in patients treated with anti-EGFR antibodies.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Among 26 cases, nine acquired high TMB at progression.
statements.note: The abstract never says which targeted agents the patients received, so it cannot settle a per-drug claim.

statements.text: Nine of the 26 microsatellite stable colorectal cancer cases developed a high tumor mutational burden at progression.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Among 26 cases, nine acquired high TMB at progression.
statements.note: These counts are reported directly.

statements.text: Tumor mutational burden was higher in tissue samples than in plasma, where few resistance alterations were found.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: TMB was higher in plasma, driven by highly subclonal acquired alterations, compared with tissue samples, which harbored few resistance alterations.
statements.note: Plasma, not tissue, carried the higher TMB, and it was tissue that harboured few resistance alterations.

statements.text: None of the three patients with acquired high tumor mutational burden who received immune checkpoint blockade responded.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Three of these patients received ICB but none had a response.
statements.note: All three treated patients failed to respond.

statements.text: MUSE-XAE pairs a nonlinear encoder with a linear decoder so that the active signatures stay interpretable.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our approach employs a hybrid architecture consisting of a nonlinear encoder that can capture nonlinear interactions among features, and a linear decoder which ensures the interpretability of the active signatures.
statements.note: This hybrid architecture is described exactly this way.

statements.text: MUSE-XAE is built from a linear encoder and a nonlinear decoder.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Our approach employs a hybrid architecture consisting of a nonlinear encoder that can capture nonlinear interactions among features, and a linear decoder which ensures the interpretability of the active signatures.
statements.note: The encoder is nonlinear and the decoder linear, the reverse of this statement.

statements.text: MUSE-XAE runs on a standard laptop without a GPU.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: MUSE-XAE software is freely available at https://github.com/compbiomed-unito/MUSE-XAE.
statements.note: Only the software's availability is given; hardware and runtime requirements are never mentioned.

statements.text: On both synthetic and real cancer datasets, MUSE-XAE recovered signature profiles with better precision and sensitivity than competing tools.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We evaluated and compared MUSE-XAE with other available tools on both synthetic and real cancer datasets and demonstrated that it achieves superior performance in terms of precision and sensitivity in recovering mutational signature profiles.
statements.note: Superior precision and sensitivity on both dataset types are reported.

statements.text: LinG3D traces clone lineages in time only, leaving out where the clones sit in the tissue.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: This routine package extends the classical lineage trees, that show cellular clone relationships in time, by adding the space component to show the locations of cellular clones within the 2D tumor tissue patch from computer simulations of tumor evolution models.
statements.note: The package's point is to add the spatial component to time-only lineage trees.

statements.text: Clones growing near blood vessels acquired drug resistance faster than clones far from the vasculature.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: For example, cells exposed to different concentrations of drugs, such as cells located near the vessels in contrast to those residing far from the vasculature, can undergo a different evolutionary path.
statements.note: Different evolutionary paths near and far from vessels are given as general motivation; the paper presents visualization routines and reports no such finding.

statements.text: LinG3D is open-source and provided in MATLAB, Python and R for visualizing clonal evolution in a two-dimensional tumor slice.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The LinG3D (Lineage Graphs in 3D) is an open-source collection of routines (in MATLAB, Python, and R) that enables spatio-temporal visualization of clonal evolution in a two-dimensional tumor slice from computer simulations of the tumor evolution models.
statements.note: The three implementations and the 2D-slice scope are stated directly.

statements.text: Besides simulated tumors with differing clone numbers, the routines were applied to an experimental colony growth assay.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The utility of LinG3D has been demonstrated through examples of simulated tumors with different number of clones and, additionally, in experimental colony growth assay.
statements.note: Both demonstration settings are reported.

statements.text: Univariate Cox regression in the TCGA-LUSC cohort identified 11 differentially expressed genes tied to senescence-related prognosis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: By univariate Cox regression analysis of gene expression data and overall survival data in the TCGA-LUSC cohort, 11 DEGs associated with prognostic cellular senescence were identified.
statements.note: The count of 11 prognostic senescence-associated genes is reported.

statements.text: TIDE and tumour mutation burden scores were more favourable in the high-risk group.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Tumour immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) score and tumour mutation burden (TMB) score were better in the low-risk group, with advantages in terms of prognostic and immunotherapy response rate.
statements.note: Both scores were better in the low-risk group.

statements.text: The ageing prognostic model is built on IGFBP1, SERPINE1, SIX1 and TRPM8.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The ageing prognostic models include genes of IGFBP1, SERPINE1, SIX1, and TRPM8.
statements.note: These four genes are named as the model's constituents.

statements.text: High-risk patients were more often current smokers than low-risk patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Tumour immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) score and tumour mutation burden (TMB) score were better in the low-risk group, with advantages in terms of prognostic and immunotherapy response rate.
statements.note: The risk groups are compared on immune and prognostic scores only; smoking status is never mentioned.

statements.text: Baseline circulating tumor DNA could be detected in fewer than half of the patients studied.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Baseline ctDNA is detectable in 94.7% of patients.
statements.note: Baseline ctDNA was detectable in 94.7% of patients, not a minority.

statements.text: Clearance of methylation-based tumor fraction on treatment went with longer time to treatment discontinuation, at a hazard ratio of 0.17.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Clearance of mTF on treatment is associated with prolonged time to treatment discontinuation (HR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.07-0.41; p < 0.0001).
statements.note: The association and its hazard ratio are reported exactly.

statements.text: Methylation-based tumor fraction was higher in patients with liver metastases than in those with bone-only disease.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: closely mirrors radiographic response and clinical outcomes in 57 patients with estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer receiving endocrine therapy with a CDK4/6 inhibitor across 350 serial plasma timepoints
statements.note: The cohort is defined by receptor status and treatment; metastatic site is never used to compare mTF levels.

statements.text: A rise in methylation-based tumor fraction came a median of 5.8 months before treatment was discontinued, outperforming mutation-based tracking.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A rise in mTF (molecular progression) precedes treatment discontinuation by a median of 5.8 months and outperforms mutation-based tracking
statements.note: The 5.8-month lead time and the comparison with mutation tracking are both reported.

statements.text: TERT promoter mutations were the alteration most frequently detected in plasma.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Commonly mutated genes in plasma and tissue, particularly TERT and TP53, were assessed using the AVENIO ctDNA platform
statements.note: The abstract names which genes were assessed but never reports how often each was detected.

statements.text: Recurrence-free survival did not differ significantly between patients with negative and positive postsurgery ctDNA.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In the overall study population, patients with negative ctDNA status in postsurgery plasma had significantly longer recurrence-free survival than those with positive ctDNA status (p = 0.01).
statements.note: The difference in recurrence-free survival was statistically significant at p = 0.01.

statements.text: ctDNA positivity fell from 46% before radical cystectomy to 23% afterwards.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The ctDNA positivity fell from 46% before surgery to 23% after surgery, and a positive postoperative result predicted recurrence independently.
statements.note: Both positivity rates are reported, along with the independent predictive value of a positive postoperative result.

statements.text: Patients converting from ctDNA-positive before surgery to negative afterwards had a median survival of 36 months against 18 months for those staying positive.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patients who were ctDNA positive before surgery and converted to ctDNA negative after surgery showed longer survival than those remaining ctDNA positive (median survival 36 vs 18 mo).
statements.note: The two median survival figures are reported for exactly these groups.

statements.text: Screening 19 marsupial genomes yielded more than 80,000 endogenous retrovirus fragments, grouped into eight clades.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We screened 19 marsupial genomes and identified over 80,000 endogenous retrovirus fragments which we classified into eight retrovirus clades.
statements.note: The genome count, fragment count and number of clades are all reported.

statements.text: Of the eight clades, three resembled betaretroviruses and five resembled gammaretroviruses.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The retroviruses were similar to either Betaretrovirus (5/8) or Gammaretrovirus (3/8) retroviruses, but formed distinct phylogenetic clades compared to extant retroviruses.
statements.note: Five clades were betaretrovirus-like and three gammaretrovirus-like, the reverse of this split.

statements.text: The endogenous retroviruses identified contribute to the high incidence of transmissible cancer in Tasmanian devils.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We therefore sought to identify and characterize Australian retroviruses through reconstruction of endogenous retroviruses from marsupial genomes, in particular the Tasmanian devil due to its high cancer incidence.
statements.note: The devil's cancer incidence is given as a reason for studying it; no link between these retroviruses and devil cancers is reported.

statements.text: One clade, MEBrv 3, lost its envelope yet stayed retrotranspositionally active and expanded across all Dasyuridae genomes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: One of the clades (MEBrv 3) lost an envelope but retained retrotranspositional activity, subsequently amplifying throughout all Dasyuridae genomes.
statements.note: Envelope loss with retained activity and amplification in Dasyuridae are all reported for MEBrv 3.

statements.text: Most transposable elements in the human genome are no longer able to move.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Transposons, transposable elements, or jumping genes, are DNA sequences that can change their position in the genome.
statements.note: Transposons are described generally and in maize; the human genome is never discussed.

statements.text: Transposable elements make up ninety percent of maize DNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Ninety percent of maize DNA is transposable elements.
statements.note: This figure is stated outright.

statements.text: McClintock's maize work was recognised with the Nobel prize in 1983.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: won her the Nobel prize in 1983
statements.note: The 1983 Nobel prize for the maize instability paper is stated.

statements.text: Transposition leaves the total amount of DNA in a cell unchanged.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Because of the nature of transposition, the process leads to mutation and changes in the amount of DNA in a cell.
statements.note: Transposition is said to change the amount of DNA in a cell.

statements.text: Base-pair resolution pairwise alignments were made between the B73 reference genome and 25 other inbred maize assemblies.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We generated base-pair resolved pairwise alignments between the B73 maize reference genome and the remaining 25 inbred maize line assemblies.
statements.note: The reference, the number of comparison assemblies and the alignment resolution are all stated.

statements.text: The structural variants identified account for differences in grain yield between the maize lines.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Structural differences between genomes are a major source of genetic variation that contributes to phenotypic differences.
statements.note: The opening frames structural variation as contributing to phenotype in general; no trait such as yield is measured here.

statements.text: Transposable elements make up under a quarter of the maize genome.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Domesticated maize is a particularly good system for exploring the impact of transposable element proliferation as over 70% of the genome is annotated as transposable elements.
statements.note: Over 70% of the maize genome is annotated as transposable elements.

statements.text: Within recently diverged regions, transposable element deletions accounted for more structural variation events and base pairs than insertions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: within these recently diverged genomic regions, deletions of transposable elements likely account for more structural variation events and base pairs than insertions
statements.note: Deletions outweighing insertions in these regions is the study's headline result.

statements.text: Mobile genetic element activity fell with longer cultivation and showed no correlation with key resistance genes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: MGEs activity increased over time and was significantly correlated with key ARGs.
statements.note: Mobile genetic element activity increased over time and correlated significantly with key resistance genes.

statements.text: Resistance gene abundance and diversity rose sharply after five years of cultivation and peaked at 10 to 20 years.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ARGs abundance and diversity increased markedly after five years and peaked at 10-20 years.
statements.note: Both the five-year rise and the 10-20 year peak are reported.

statements.text: Path analysis pointed to improved soil properties as the main direct driver of resistance gene accumulation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Path analysis identified improved soil properties as the primary direct driver of ARGs accumulation
statements.note: This is the direct driver identified by the path analysis.

statements.text: Rice grown in the long-cultivated fields carried antibiotic resistance genes in its grain.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings highlight the need to integrate ARGs monitoring into soil health assessments for sustainable management of reclaimed saline-sodic lands.
statements.note: The study measures the soil resistome only and reports nothing about the rice plants themselves.

statements.text: Breast tumors carrying MAP3K1 or MAP2K4 mutations respond better to JNK-pathway inhibitors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study highlights the dual regulatory mechanisms controlling FRA1 expression and offers insights into breast cancer heterogeneity, with potential implications for targeted therapy and patient stratification.
statements.note: Implications for targeted therapy are raised in general terms; no drug response was measured.

statements.text: MAP3K1 and MAP2K4 mutations in breast cancer were mostly loss-of-function, mutually exclusive with TP53 alterations and enriched in ER-positive tumors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: MAP3K1 and MAP2K4 were identified as frequently mutated in BRCA, with mutation spectra dominated by loss-of-function alterations. These mutations exhibited mutual exclusivity with TP53 alterations and were enriched in ER + tumors.
statements.note: All three features of the mutation pattern are reported.

statements.text: Loss of MAP3K1 or MAP2K4 lowered JNK2 phosphorylation, blunted p53 activation at Ser15 and raised FOSL1 expression.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: MAP3K1/MAP2K4 loss led to reduced JNK2 phosphorylation, impaired p53 activation at Ser15, and subsequent upregulation of FOSL1 (encoding FRA1), promoting tumor proliferation and metastasis.
statements.note: This is the reported mechanistic chain from kinase loss to FOSL1 upregulation.

statements.text: Expressing dominant-negative MAP2K4 in xenografts suppressed tumor growth and lung metastasis.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In vivo, MKK4DN (dominant-negative MAP2K4) expression enhanced tumor growth and lung metastasis, accompanied by decreased phospho-JNK/p53 and increased FRA1.
statements.note: Dominant-negative MAP2K4 enhanced, not suppressed, growth and lung metastasis.

statements.text: Three of the 15 enrolled patients met the composite primary endpoint, and the overall response rate was 6.7%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: One patient had a partial response (ORR 6.7%) and was without progression at 6 months (PFS6) whereas two other patients achieved PFS6 alone. In total, 3 out of 15 patients met the primary endpoint (3/15; 20%).
statements.note: One partial response plus two patients with PFS6 gives the reported 3 of 15.

statements.text: The fall in plasma (R)-2HG was larger in glioma patients than in those with other tumor types.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Pharmacodynamic studies demonstrated combining ivosidenib and nivolumab significantly decreased the plasma (R)-2HG concentration and correlated with clinical benefit.
statements.note: The 2HG decrease is reported for the cohort as a whole and tied to clinical benefit, never broken down by tumor type.

statements.text: Adding nivolumab to ivosidenib produced clearly greater anti-tumor activity than ivosidenib alone.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the combination of ivosidenib and nivolumab was safe however demonstrated similar anti-tumor activity (predominantly as disease stabilization) compared with that previously described for ivosidenib monotherapy
statements.note: Activity of the combination was similar to that previously described for ivosidenib monotherapy.

statements.text: Leukopenia and rash were the most common adverse events, each in 67% of patients, and median progression-free survival was 1.94 months.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The median PFS was 1.94 months. The most common treatment adverse events were leukopenia (67%), rash (67%), diarrhea (33%), nausea (27%), and QTC prolongation (27%).
statements.note: Both the adverse event frequencies and the median PFS are reported exactly.

statements.text: The genes narG and manCcore were present in all five isolates, while aaiB was restricted to the bloodstream isolates.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Comparative analyses revealed distinct genetic profiles: aaiB (T6SS) was present in all isolates, whereas narG and manCcore were exclusive to bloodstream isolates.
statements.note: aaiB was in all isolates and narG and manCcore were the bloodstream-exclusive genes, the reverse of this statement.

statements.text: Five isolates from the sputum and blood of one pediatric cystic fibrosis patient were sequenced and analysed in silico.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: five B. cenocepacia isolates recovered from sputum and blood samples of a pediatric CF patient who developed CS were sequenced and analyzed in silico
statements.note: The isolate count, sample types and single-patient origin are stated.

statements.text: The patient received meropenem before the bloodstream isolates were collected.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings describe a novel B. cenocepacia sequence type associated with fatal CS and highlight the high genomic plasticity of this species, reinforcing the importance of genomic surveillance to detect emerging variants and improve clinical management in CF.
statements.note: Genomic findings and the fatal course are reported, but nothing about which antibiotics the patient received.

statements.text: The isolates belonged to a newly identified sequence type, ST2424, outside any known clonal complex.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A novel sequence type (ST2424), not associated with any known clonal complex, was identified.
statements.note: ST2424 is reported as novel and unassigned to a clonal complex.

statements.text: Right-sided colon tumors released more ctDNA than left-sided tumors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: RevMan 5.3 was used to conduct meta-analyses and subgroup investigations classified by tumor population, two-year or three-year DFS, and tumor location.
statements.note: Tumor location served as a subgroup for survival analyses; ctDNA levels by tumor side are never compared.

statements.text: In the pre-operative analyses, higher ctDNA levels were significantly associated with shorter disease-free and overall survival.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients who had higher ctDNA levels had considerably lower DFS and OS, but these differences were not statistically significant.
statements.note: The pre-operative differences were not statistically significant.

statements.text: The meta-analysis pooled 11 trials covering 605 patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The analysis included 11 trials conducted with 605 individuals.
statements.note: These are the trial and patient counts included.

statements.text: High post-operative ctDNA went with worse disease-free and overall survival in every subgroup examined.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patients with high levels of ctDNA had worse DFS and OS, regardless of the tumor population, two-year DFS, three-year DFS, or tumor location.
statements.note: The association held across all the subgroups analysed.

statements.text: ctDNA was detected in 47 of the 71 patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Among the 71 included patients, ctDNA was detected in 47 patients (66.2%).
statements.note: These detection counts are reported directly.

statements.text: Liver tumor volume correlated more strongly with ctDNA quantity than total tumor volume did, with Spearman coefficients of 0.500 against 0.353.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: There was a significant correlation of total and liver TV with ctDNA quantity, with Spearman's ρ of 0.353 (p = 0.01) and 0.500 (p < 0.001), respectively.
statements.note: The two correlation coefficients are reported in exactly this order for total and liver volume.

statements.text: The two methylated markers HOXD8 and POU4F1 were detected at similar frequencies.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: ctDNA quantity at baseline (before chemotherapy initiation) was assessed by droplet-based digital PCR targeting two methylated markers (HOXD8 and POU4F1).
statements.note: The two markers are named but their individual detection rates are never reported.

statements.text: Patients in whom ctDNA was detected had smaller total tumor volumes than those without detectable ctDNA.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Total and liver TV were higher in patients with detected ctDNA (129.5 vs. 31.8 mL, p = 0.002 and 18 vs. 1 mL, p < 0.001, respectively).
statements.note: Tumor volumes were higher, not smaller, in patients with detectable ctDNA.

statements.text: Distant progression occurred in 10 of 52 adults, seven of whom had a primary spinal tumor location.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Distant progression including leptomeningeal disease occurred in 10 out of 52 adult patients (19%), seven of which had a primary spinal tumor location (70%, p < 0.001)
statements.note: Both counts are reported, with the spinal predominance significant at p < 0.001.

statements.text: Distant progression was more frequent in adults than in children with H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: It has been most extensively characterized in children and adolescents and continues to pose significant challenges to treating physicians due to its growth along the midline structures of the brain and its ability to progress distantly leading to poor prognosis.
statements.note: The cohort is adults only, and no paediatric comparison group is analysed.

statements.text: Patients with distant progression had a median progression-free survival of 4.5 months against 13 months for the rest of the cohort.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: distant progression was associated with worse progression free survival (PFS) (4.5 vs. 13 months; p = 0.037)
statements.note: These median PFS values and the significance level are reported.

statements.text: A methylation-based signature significantly predicted which patients would develop distant progression.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: However, we could not identify a genetic or methylation-based signature that was significantly correlated with the occurrence of distant progression.
statements.note: No genetic or methylation signature correlated significantly with distant progression.

statements.text: SMARCA4 alterations were most frequent in thymic epithelial tumors at 10.7% and in non-small cell lung cancer at 7.1%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: SMARCA4 alterations were most frequent in thymic epithelial tumors (10.7%), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC; 7.1%), bladder cancer (5.6%), and cervical cancer (5%).
statements.note: These are the top two tumor types and frequencies reported.

statements.text: In the phase I trial of PRT3789, clinical benefit was seen in patients with biallelic class 1 alterations and loss of BRG1 expression.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In a phase I trial of the BRM degrader PRT3789, patients with monoallelic class 2 SMARCA4 alterations and preserved BRG1 expression saw clinical benefit, including one who attained a complete response.
statements.note: Benefit was seen with monoallelic class 2 alterations and preserved BRG1 expression.

statements.text: Patients with SMARCA4-altered tumors had shorter survival on platinum-based therapy than patients with wild-type SMARCA4.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Clinical outcomes were evaluated in selected tumor cohorts treated with platinum-based therapy or immune checkpoint blockade.
statements.note: The abstract says these outcomes were evaluated but never gives the result or its direction.

statements.text: Class 1 alterations were about four times as common as class 2 alterations, at 2.9% versus 0.7% of tumors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Class 1 and class 2 alterations occurred in 2.9% and 0.7% of tumors, respectively.
statements.note: Both class frequencies are reported, and 2.9% is roughly four times 0.7%.

statements.text: PD-L1 expression in the tumor or its microenvironment showed no association with benefit from treatment.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The PD-L1 expression level in tumor or tumor microenvironment was not associated with treatment benefit.
statements.note: The absence of an association with PD-L1 expression is reported.

statements.text: Patients with HPV-positive tumors did better on pembrolizumab than those with HPV-negative tumors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We evaluated various blood and tissue-based biomarkers in the context of immune checkpoint blockade-based treatment to find suitable response biomarkers in a clinical trial cohort of patients with rmHNSCC.
statements.note: The biomarkers assessed are inflammatory and immune ones; HPV status is never mentioned.

statements.text: Patients without the inflammatory high-risk markers did poorly on pembrolizumab.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients lacking these high-risk markers performed remarkably well on inhibition of immune checkpoints with pembrolizumab.
statements.note: Patients lacking the high-risk markers did remarkably well on pembrolizumab.

statements.text: High cell-free DNA levels, elevated IL-6 and high peripheral neutrophil counts all went with poor clinical outcomes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: inflammation-related markers such as IL-6, high peripheral neutrophils and high levels of cell-free DNA, as well as markers related to adaptive immune dysfunction such as altered T cell dynamics and secretion of immune checkpoint molecules, were associated with poor clinical outcomes
statements.note: All three inflammatory markers are listed among those associated with poor outcomes.

statements.text: The analysis showed that most internal copy-number events are under focal selection.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: simultaneously showing that most internal copy-number events are not subject to focal selection
statements.note: Most internal copy-number events are reported as not subject to focal selection.

statements.text: SPICE was applied to 5,966 TCGA samples and tracked shifts in event types before and after whole-genome duplication.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Applied to 5,966 samples from the TCGA dataset, SPICE quantifies the full spectrum of SCNA events, recapitulates known mutational processes, and tracks systematic shifts in event types before and after whole-genome duplication (WGD).
statements.note: The sample count and the WGD analysis are both reported.

statements.text: Newly identified loci were confirmed by CRISPR screens in cancer cell lines.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These results establish a unified framework that deconvolves copy-number profiles into their underlying evolutionary events and greatly expand the catalogue of loci implicated in cancer development.
statements.note: The work is computational throughout; no experimental follow-up of the new loci is described.

statements.text: The selection model identified 460 loci under selection, strongly enriched for known oncogenes and tumour suppressors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This analysis reveals 460 loci under selection which are highly enriched for known oncogenes and tumour suppressors
statements.note: The count of 460 selected loci and their enrichment are reported.

statements.text: Strains carrying more transposons were more virulent on their host plants.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Furthermore, despite only 5 % of genes being dispensable, SVs often had a stronger impact than other variants across 14 life history traits measured in 103 distinct strains.
statements.note: Trait variation is attributed to structural variants in general; transposon load is never compared with virulence.

statements.text: A graphical pan-genome of the host-generalist pathogen was assembled from 25 high-quality genomes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We use 25 high quality genomes to create a graphical pan-genome of the globally distributed host-generalist crop pathogen
statements.note: The pan-genome was built from 25 high-quality genomes.

statements.text: Recombination and transposons contributed to structural variant diversity in the same way, with no separable effects.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we show that recombination and transposons make distinct contributions to SV diversity
statements.note: Their contributions to structural variant diversity are reported as distinct.

statements.text: Although only 5% of genes were dispensable, structural variants often had a stronger effect than other variants across 14 life history traits in 103 strains.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: despite only 5 % of genes being dispensable, SVs often had a stronger impact than other variants across 14 life history traits measured in 103 distinct strains
statements.note: The dispensable-gene fraction, trait count and strain count are all reported.
